oracle.endpoint_local_exhaustive_truth: pass for natural, two-arm final, exhaustive challenger best, model output, v1 output, fixed64 output and fixed128 output in all 40 cases

interpretation.primary: The single frozen development model passed its untouched n=16 usefulness rule, recovering 23/26 = 88.46% of exhaustive challenger gain while using 20.17% of exhaustive challenger BDD compilations with zero harm relative to the retained two-arm incumbent.
interpretation.comparison: On this split the frozen model and the hand-coded v1 policy made identical quality/compute decisions. Fixed64 recovered only 13/26 gain; fixed128 recovered the same 13/26 while using more BDD compilations than the model.
interpretation.calibration_warning: The apparent aggregate success is dominated by one immediate gain-20 case that required no learned continuation decision. Among the 39 actual index65 model decisions there were only two positive labels; the model caught one and missed one, so conditional positive recall was only 50%. Do not infer calibrated rare-tail prediction from aggregate gain recovery.
interpretation.failure_case: The missed Erdős seed 891305 had eventual gain3 only at certificate index359, gap65=18 and frozen model probability0.0407. This remains heavy-tail evidence against interpreting low model probability as a negative certificate.
interpretation.scope: Synthetic positive-monotone graph 2-CNF ROBDD ordering only. This validates aggregate allocation on one holdout, not tail-probability calibration or theorem-proving transfer.
